chapters.title: Okay fine, the fix (Bom made me)

text.first-impression: Gyeong, strangers feel slightly intimidated, then slightly impressed. You're direct, decisive, and you don't fake interest in anything. Ten seconds in, they know whether you like them, because your face has no privacy settings. You're loyal, fair, and you'd fight for your people without being asked. What they don't see right away: you're actually soft about the few you love. Very soft. You just guard it like a bank vault with a moat and a slightly scary security guard, who is also you. Maybe lower the drawbridge occasionally.
text.your-red-flag: Let's start with the red one: you're blunt. Sometimes surgically. You say the true thing with zero padding and then can't understand why someone's upset. I was just being honest. Yes. Honesty without kindness is just a sharp object being waved around a kitchen. You also see the world in black and white, and gray makes you angry. Most of life is gray. Annoying, I know. You can keep the blade. Just learn to put it back in its sheath when you're having a conversation instead of a duel. Same truth, gentler delivery. Still counts.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: When you love someone, you're loyal to the bone. Once you choose, you choose, and that's rare and wonderful. But you can be hard to approach and harder to argue with. Your sabotage is treating disagreements like battles to win, and cutting people off fast when they disappoint you. One mistake and the file is closed and archived. Some people deserve a second look. Also, say soft things sometimes. Your partner knows you'd fight a bear for them. They would also like a compliment about their hair. Both matter. Give them both. You have plenty of each.
text.friends-and-work: In any team you're decisive and brilliant in a crisis. You also have zero patience for incompetence, and it shows: on your face, in meetings, in the way you type. With friends you're the one who'd help hide the evidence, metaphorically, of course. Loyal forever. But you drop people quickly when they cross a line, and your lines aren't always visible to anyone except you. Tell people where the lines are. They can't respect a boundary they've never been shown. A quick heads-up costs you one sentence and saves a whole friendship. Very efficient. You'll love it.
text.the-lie: The line you repeat when nobody's listening: I don't care what people think. You care a great deal about what your people think. You care about being respected and being seen as fair. You also tell yourself that being tough means not getting hurt. It doesn't. It means you get hurt and don't show it, which is a completely different thing and much heavier to carry. Ask yourself who's protecting you while you're busy protecting everyone else. If the answer is nobody, that's worth fixing. Let one person in on the armor.
text.the-fix: Fine, the fix, at Bom's insistence. Before saying the true thing, add one kind sentence in front of it. Ask one question before you deliver a verdict. Allow one second chance this year, where it's actually deserved. In love, say the soft thing: I appreciate you. It's not weakness. It's precision, applied to feelings. You're the most loyal person most people will ever meet. Imagine if they also felt safe disagreeing with you. That would make you basically unbeatable, which I know you'd enjoy. Start with the kind sentence. Start today. Start with someone who'll be very confused.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, you called their haircut 'a choice'. They cried.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Honesty without kindness is a knife in a nice outfit.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also, one mistake and you archive people. Bit much.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong is the most loyal friend ever, though.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: True. Add one kind sentence before the verdict. Every time.

spring.intro: Spring Gyeong, Wood was in command when you arrived and Metal cuts Wood, so you were born facing a forest and holding an axe. You're decisive, energetic and slightly dangerous to be around when there's a task. People see a natural leader. Your friends know you'll take over the group trip whether anyone asked or not. Your red flag is charging ahead and calling it efficiency. You chop first and check the map later. In love you pursue hard and then lose interest when there's nothing left to conquer. At work you get things done and leave a few bruised egos behind. The fix: before acting, ask two people's opinions. Then actually use one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You took over the group trip planning without asking. Again, Gyeong. We noticed.

summer.intro: Summer Gyeong, you were born while Fire was in charge and Fire melts Metal, so you were forged under pressure and you've decided that makes you unbreakable. You're tough, loyal and very proud of not needing anyone. People see someone strong. Your friends know you'd rather walk home on a sprained ankle than ask for a lift. Your red flag is armor. You don't show hurt, so people assume you can't be hurt, and then they're careless with you. In love partners can't reach you. At work you take the hardest jobs and never admit they're hard. The fix: ask for help with something small. Then say thank you. That's it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Refusing a lift on a sprained ankle isn't strength, Gyeong. It's limping with pride.

autumn.intro: Autumn-born Gyeong: Metal ran the season and doubled your element. You're the sword fully drawn: honest, loyal and blunt to a degree that occasionally makes waiters nervous. People see someone who tells it like it is. Your friends see someone who has never once softened a sentence. Your red flag is honesty without delivery. You think being right is enough, but the truth landed like a slap. In love you say exactly what you think, then wonder why they're defensive. At work you're respected and slightly feared. The fix: add one kind sentence before every honest one. It doesn't make you fake. It makes you heard.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: I'm brutal, but even I warm up first. You don't, Gyeong. Learn from me.

winter.intro: Winter Gyeong, you were born while Water was in charge and Metal generates Water, so your strength comes out as cold logic. You're the friend who answers a sad text with a five-step plan. People see someone sharp and composed. Your friends know you love them deeply and show it by fixing their tax return. Your red flag is solving instead of feeling. Someone shares a problem, you hand them a solution and miss the moment. In love partners feel helped but not held. At work you're brilliant and slightly intimidating. The fix: next time someone vents, say that sounds hard and nothing else for one full minute. Painful. Worth it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They said they were sad. You sent a spreadsheet. That's not comfort, Gyeong.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Gyeong, you're ore inside a mountain: Earth feeds Metal, so you arrived well backed and very sure of yourself. People see strength. Your friends see someone who argues with a waiter about principle. Your red flag is righteousness. In love you'd rather be fair than warm, and partners feel judged instead of held. At work you're right a lot, and you make sure everyone knows. The fix: let someone else be right this week and say so out loud.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Gyeong, being correct and being kind aren't rivals. Try both.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Gyeong. Your metal is reinforced on all sides, which makes you tough, blunt and quite proud of how little you care what people think. The blind spot: you mistake bluntness for honesty and stubbornness for loyalty. You'll defend a bad decision because you made it. In love you fight to win, not to understand. With friends you say what everyone's thinking, often at the worst possible moment. The fix: before you speak, ask whether it's true, kind and necessary. Two out of three is fine. One out of three, stay quiet.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Gyeong, so you act tough with less support behind it, which means a lot of bluffing. The blind spot: you swing between doormat and explosion. You let things slide to look easygoing, then cut someone off over something tiny because the pile got too high. In love you go along, go along, then leave. At work you don't push back until the day you quit. The fix: say one small no early instead of one giant no late. Little edges, often. Fewer explosions.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything feels urgent, out loud or only on the inside, and your feelings arrive with sirens on even when nobody else can hear them. You're bright company, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the color, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyze it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair color twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
